subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Problem of Induction: Hume's Bombshell
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Problem of Induction: Hume's Bombshell.

hook.text: The sun has risen every day for 4.5 billion years. Can you prove it will rise tomorrow? David Hume said no.

buildup.text: In 1739, Hume argued that past patterns can never logically guarantee future events.

discovery.text: We assume nature is uniform — that the future will resemble the past. But that assumption itself is inductive.

twist.text: It's circular: we trust induction because it worked before — which is itself an inductive argument.

climax.text: No philosopher has ever fully solved the problem of induction. We just trust it because it works.

punchline.text: Science's foundation has no foundation. It just works.

quiz.question: What did Hume argue about induction?
options: Past patterns can't logically guarantee future events

details.summary: David Hume argued that inductive reasoning cannot be logically justified: the fact that the sun rose every past morning does not guarantee it will rise tomorrow. Past regularities provide no logical proof of future ones.
details.whyItMatters: Hume's problem undermines the logical foundation of science itself and has never been fully resolved, only pragmatically sidestepped.
takeaways: Past observations cannot logically guarantee future outcomes
Induction relies on an unprovable assumption of uniformity
Science works despite—not because of—logical justification for induction

faq.question: What exactly is the problem of induction?
faq.answer: You cannot use past experience to prove that the future will resemble the past without assuming the very principle you are trying to prove, creating a circular argument.

faq.question: How does science function if induction cannot be logically justified?
faq.answer: Scientists adopt induction as a pragmatic method that has worked reliably, supported by statistical theory and falsification, even though its ultimate logical foundation remains unresolved.
